rule: Never hit external third-party URLs (e.g. example.com) in tests; use the project's local HTTP test server instead to prevent flaky CI failures.

evidence.quote:
These tests reach out to `example.com` but they should probably use a local echo server instead.

Testing against 3rd party services should only be done when necessary, because it causes sporadic test failures when a site is down. Tests can also hit rate limits or IP bans in CI very easily.

These tests are mostly just mimicking the current implementation to test the internal utilities. I would prefer that they use a server and Ky itself, as most of the other tests do, to echo back the de-serialized body length that it receives and maybe also the `Content-Length`, for example, and then run assertions for different body types based on that and the `totalBytes` parameter. Thus making the assertions more realistic and less coupled to the implementation.

rule: Guard new browser-API calls (e.g. `AbortSignal.any`) with the same feature-detection checks already present in the codebase; never introduce an unguarded call that regresses older environments.

evidence.quote: The new merge logic always calls `AbortSignal.any` when more than one signal is present. In browsers where `AbortSignal.any` is still missing (the rest of the codebase explicitly checks `supportsAbortSignal` for this reason), this line will throw `TypeError: AbortSignal.any is not a function` whenever instance options with a `signal` are merged with request options. This is a regression from previous behavior and breaks environments that Ky otherwise supports. Consider guarding the call behind the same feature check or providing a fallback.
This should also only be done for Node.js. I don't want to risk some weird behavior in browsers where it's not needed.
